text.fr: 1. i* : des acteurs intentionnels, deux modèles
text.en: 1. i*: intentional actors, two models

text.fr: 1.1 Définition : l’acteur intentionnel
text.en: 1.1 Definition: the intentional actor

text.fr: **[[term-istar|i*]]** (Yu, 1997) : un cadre de modélisation pour la **phase amont** de l’ingénierie des exigences. Son concept central est l’**acteur intentionnel** : il a des buts, des croyances, des capacités et des engagements, et il **dépend** d’autres acteurs pour atteindre des buts, faire exécuter des tâches, obtenir des ressources. Deux modèles : le **modèle SD** (*Strategic Dependency*) décrit les dépendances **entre** les acteurs ; le **modèle SR** (*Strategic Rationale*) décrit les intérêts de chaque acteur et la façon de les satisfaire.
text.en: **[[term-istar|i*]]** (Yu, 1997): a modelling framework for the **early phase** of requirements engineering. Its central concept is the **intentional actor**: it has goals, beliefs, abilities and commitments, and it **depends** on other actors for goals to be achieved, tasks to be performed and resources to be furnished. Two models: the **SD model** (*Strategic Dependency*) describes the dependencies **among** actors; the **SR model** (*Strategic Rationale*) describes each actor’s interests and how they might be addressed.

src.quote: Organizational actors are viewed as having intentional properties such as goals, beliefs, abilities, and commitments
Actors depend on each other for goals to be achieved, tasks to be performed, and resources to be furnished
The Strategic Dependency (SD) model is used to describe the dependency relationships among various actors in an organizational context
The Strategic Rationale (SR) model is used to describe stakeholder interests and concerns, and how they might be addressed by various configurations of systems and environments

text.fr: 1.2 Pourquoi i* : la phase amont
text.en: 1.2 Why i*: the early phase

text.fr: Pourquoi i* ? Les modèles d’exigences habituels décrivent le **quoi** ; i* sert à comprendre le **pourquoi** avant de rédiger les exigences. La phase amont modélise les intérêts des parties prenantes et la façon dont chaque configuration du système et de son environnement les sert ou les compromet ; la phase aval vise la complétude, la cohérence et la vérification des exigences.
text.en: Why i*? Usual requirements models describe the **what**; i* helps understand the **why** before writing requirements. The early phase models stakeholder interests and how each system-and-environment configuration addresses or compromises them; the late phase focuses on completeness, consistency and verification of requirements.

src.quote: They tend to focus on the “what” rather than the “why”
the early phase aims to model and analyze stakeholder interests and how they might be addressed, or compromised, by various system-and-environment alternatives
which focuses on completeness, consistency, and automated verification of requirements

text.fr: 1.3 Les deux modèles : SD et SR
text.en: 1.3 The two models: SD and SR

rows.en: The dependencies **among** actors (who depends on whom, for what); it hides what happens inside each actor

rows.fr: Comprendre une organisation, existante ou proposée
rows.en: Understanding an organisation, existing or proposed

rows.en: The **inside** of each actor: goals, tasks, resources, soft goals and their links

src.quote: It shows external (but nevertheless intentional) relationships among actors, while hiding the intentional constructs within each actor
the Strategic Rationale model provides a more detailed level of modelling by looking “inside” actors to model internal intentional relationships
Only when one needs to reason about alternative configurations would one need to make explicit the goals and criteria for such deliberations

text.fr: i* (Yu) = des acteurs **intentionnels** et leurs dépendances, pour la **phase amont** (le pourquoi), pas pour la vérification. **SD** = les dépendances entre acteurs ; **SR** = l’intérieur de chaque acteur, quand il faut comparer des alternatives.
text.en: i* (Yu) = **intentional** actors and their dependencies, for the **early phase** (the why), not for verification. **SD** = dependencies among actors; **SR** = the inside of each actor, when alternatives must be compared.

text.fr: 2. Le modèle SD : quatre types de dépendance
text.en: 2. The SD model: four types of dependency

text.fr: 2.1 Depender, dependee, opportunité, vulnérabilité
text.en: 2.1 Depender, dependee, opportunity, vulnerability

text.fr: Une dépendance relie un **depender** (celui qui dépend) à un **dependee** (celui dont il dépend). En dépendant d’un autre, un acteur peut atteindre ce qu’il n’atteindrait pas seul (une **opportunité**) ; il devient **vulnérable** si l’autre ne fournit pas. Une dépendance **critique** est marquée d’un **X**. Le **type** de la dépendance dit quelle liberté on laisse au dependee.
text.en: A dependency links a **depender** (the one who depends) to a **dependee** (the one depended on). By depending on another, an actor may achieve what it could not achieve alone (an **opportunity**); it becomes **vulnerable** if the other does not deliver. A **critical** dependency is marked with an **X**. The dependency **type** says how much freedom the dependee is given.

src.quote: By depending on others, an actor may be able to achieve goals that are difficult or impossible to achieve on its own
an actor becomes vulnerable if the depended-on actors do not deliver
the meeting initiator depends critically (marked with an “X” in the graphical notation) on their attendance
Dependency types are used to differentiate among the kinds of relationships between depender and dependee, involving different types of freedom and constraint

text.en: 2.2 The four types: goal, task, resource, softgoal

src.quote: The meeting initiator delegates much of the work of meeting scheduling to the meeting scheduler
The scheduler expects the meeting initiator to enter the date range by following a specific procedure
to enter availability information in a particular format. This is modelled as a task dependency on participants

text.fr: Ce que le modèle fait voir : l’initiateur **délègue** la planification à l’ordonnanceur (une opportunité : il n’a plus à atteindre ce but lui-même, mais il devient vulnérable si l’ordonnanceur échoue). En revanche, la présence des participants importants **n’est pas déléguée** : c’est l’initiateur, pas l’ordonnanceur, qui a un **enjeu** à ce qu’ils viennent.
text.en: What the model reveals: the initiator **delegates** scheduling to the scheduler (an opportunity: it no longer has to achieve this goal itself, but becomes vulnerable if the scheduler fails). However, the attendance of important participants is **not delegated**: the initiator, not the scheduler, has a **stake** in their attendance.

src.quote: The meeting initiator delegates much of the work of meeting scheduling to the meeting scheduler
represents an opportunity for the meeting initiator not to have to achieve this goal himself
the meeting initiator would become vulnerable to the failure of the meeting scheduler in achieving this goal
It is the meeting initiator (not the meeting scheduler) who has a stake in having participants attend the meeting

text.fr: 4 types, selon la liberté laissée : **but** (le dependee choisit comment), **tâche** (manière imposée), **ressource** (fournir une entité ; le depender garde la résolution), **soft goal** (le depender juge ce qui suffit). X = critique. Dépendre = opportunité + vulnérabilité.
text.en: 4 types, by the freedom given: **goal** (the dependee chooses how), **task** (imposed way), **resource** (furnish an entity; the depender keeps the problem solving), **softgoal** (the depender judges what is enough). X = critical. Depending = opportunity + vulnerability.

text.fr: 3. Les soft goals et le satisficing
text.en: 3. Softgoals and satisficing

text.fr: 3.1 Définition et satisficing
text.en: 3.1 Definition and satisficing

text.fr: Un **[[term-soft-goal|soft goal]]** (i*, KAOS) est un but dont la satisfaction ne peut pas être établie de façon tranchée. On parle de *satisficing* : les sous-buts doivent atteindre le but parent dans des limites acceptables ; chez Yu, il s’agit de trouver des solutions « suffisamment bonnes ».
text.en: A **[[term-soft-goal|soft goal]]** (i*, KAOS) is a goal whose satisfaction cannot be established in a clear-cut way. This is called *satisficing*: subgoals must achieve the parent goal within acceptable limits; for Yu, it means finding “good enough” solutions.

src.quote: soft goals, whose satisfaction cannot be established in a clear-cut sense
goal satisficing is introduced to express that subgoals are expected to achieve the parent goal within acceptable limits, rather than absolutely
The notion of softgoal draws on the concept of satisficing [33], which refers to finding solutions that are “good enough”

text.fr: 3.2 À quoi servent les soft goals
text.en: 3.2 What softgoals are for

text.fr: Les soft goals disent pourquoi on choisit une alternative plutôt qu’une autre, et une routine dont les soft goals ne sont pas satisfaits de façon suffisante **n’est pas viable**. Le cours y fait écho : Zave et Jackson (« Four dark corners ») citent les exigences « soft » de Yu, vagues et imprécises, comme un système « sûr », « fiable » ou « facile à utiliser ».
text.en: Softgoals tell why one alternative is chosen over another, and a routine whose softgoals are not satisficed **is not viable**. The course echoes this: Zave and Jackson (“Four dark corners”) cite Yu’s “soft” requirements, vague and imprecise, such as a system being “secure”, “reliable” or “easy to use”.

src.quote: From the softgoals, one can tell why one alternative may be chosen over others
When softgoals are not satisficed, the routine is not viable
“Soft” requirements as discussed by Yu et al. [1995] are “soft” for two reasons
They may be vague and imprecise, such as requirements that a
system be “secure,” “reliable,” or “easy to use.” Until they are precise enough to be formalized

text.fr: 3.3 Le piège de l’annale 2013 (Q3)
text.en: 3.3 The 2013 exam trap (Q3)

text.fr: Annale 2013, Q3 : les soft goals « ne peuvent **jamais** être satisfaits puisqu’on n’a pas de critère mesurable ». Corrigé proposé : **FAUX** : un soft goal est satisfait de façon **suffisante** (*satisficed*), selon un jugement, même sans critère tranché. « Jamais » doit t’alerter.
text.en: 2013 exam, Q3: soft goals “can **never** be satisfied since there is no measurable criterion”. Proposed answer: **FALSE**: a soft goal is satisfied **sufficiently** (*satisficed*), by judgement, even without a clear-cut criterion. “Never” should alert you.

src.quote: sont des buts qui ne peuvent jamais être satisfaits puisqu'on n'a pas de critère mesurable
soft goals, whose satisfaction cannot be established in a clear-cut sense
goal satisficing is introduced to express that subgoals are expected to achieve the parent goal within acceptable limits, rather than absolutely

text.fr: Soft goal = pas de critère tranché, mais satisfait de façon suffisante (*satisficing*) : « jamais satisfait » est faux. Il sert à choisir entre alternatives ; des soft goals non satisfaits rendent la routine non viable.
text.en: Softgoal = no clear-cut criterion, but satisficed (“good enough”): “never satisfied” is false. It helps choose between alternatives; unsatisficed softgoals make the routine not viable.

text.fr: 4. Méthode : construire un modèle i*
text.en: 4. Method: building an i* model

text.fr: 4.1 Les étapes
text.en: 4.1 The steps

title.fr: Construire un modèle i* (SD, puis SR)
title.en: Building an i* model (SD, then SR)

do.fr: Lister les acteurs : les parties prenantes **et** le système à construire.
do.en: List the actors: the stakeholders **and** the system to be built.

why.fr: i* décrit comment le système s’insère dans son environnement organisationnel : chez Yu, l’ordonnanceur est un acteur du modèle.
why.en: i* describes how the system is embedded in its organisational environment: in Yu’s model, the scheduler is an actor.

do.fr: Pour chaque acteur, se demander : de qui dépend-il, et pour quoi ?
do.en: For each actor, ask: whom does it depend on, and for what?

why.fr: Noter les dépendances entre acteurs donne les « pourquoi ».
why.en: Noting the dependencies among actors gives the “whys”.

do.fr: Typer chaque dépendance par la liberté laissée : le dependee choisit comment → **but** ; la manière est imposée → **tâche** ; il fournit seulement une entité → **ressource** ; pas de critère tranché, le depender juge → **soft goal**.
do.en: Type each dependency by the freedom given: the dependee chooses how → **goal**; the way is imposed → **task**; it only furnishes an entity → **resource**; no clear-cut criterion, the depender judges → **softgoal**.

why.fr: Les types de dépendance distinguent des degrés de liberté et de contrainte différents.
why.en: Dependency types distinguish different degrees of freedom and constraint.

do.fr: Marquer les dépendances critiques (X) et relever, pour chaque acteur, opportunités et vulnérabilités.
do.en: Mark critical dependencies (X) and note, for each actor, opportunities and vulnerabilities.

why.fr: C’est l’analyse que permet le modèle SD.
why.en: This is the analysis the SD model enables.

do.fr: S’il faut comparer des solutions, passer au SR (partie 5) : buts internes, moyens (moyens-fins), décompositions, puis contributions + / − de chaque alternative aux soft goals.
do.en: If solutions must be compared, move to the SR (part 5): internal goals, means (means-ends), decompositions, then each alternative’s + / − contributions to softgoals.

why.fr: Les soft goals disent pourquoi on choisit une alternative plutôt qu’une autre.
why.en: Softgoals tell why one alternative is chosen over another.

src.quote: To provide a deeper level of understanding about how the proposed meeting scheduler might be embedded in the organizational environment
By noting the dependencies that actors have on one another, one can obtain a better understanding of the “whys”
Dependency types are used to differentiate among the kinds of relationships between depender and dependee, involving different types of freedom and constraint
This allows analysis of opportunity and vulnerability
From the softgoals, one can tell why one alternative may be chosen over others

text.fr: 4.3 Le piège : tout typer en « but »
text.en: 4.3 The trap: typing everything as a “goal”

text.fr: Piège : tout typer en « but ». Le type se décide par deux questions : **qui choisit comment ?** (dependee → but ; manière imposée → tâche) et **qui juge que c’est suffisant ?** (le depender, sans critère tranché → soft goal). Un mot vague de l’énoncé (fidèle, intuitive, respectueux) signale un soft goal.
text.en: Trap: typing everything as a “goal”. The type is decided by two questions: **who chooses how?** (dependee → goal; imposed way → task) and **who judges it is enough?** (the depender, without a clear-cut criterion → softgoal). A vague word in the case (faithful, intuitive, respectful) signals a softgoal.

statement.en:
Yu compares two SD models of meeting scheduling: without and then with a computer-based scheduler.
1. Which dependency does the initiator create towards the scheduler, and of which type?
2. Which dependency does the scheduler create towards the initiator, and of which type?
3. Is the “assured attendance” dependency on important participants delegated to the scheduler? Why?
4. Which opportunity and which vulnerability does the scheduler bring to the initiator?

hints.fr: Relis le tableau des 4 types : qui choisit comment ? qui a l’enjeu ?
hints.en: Reread the table of the 4 types: who chooses how? who has the stake?

solution.fr:
1. Une dépendance de **but** (MeetingBeScheduled) : l’initiateur délègue la planification et ne se soucie pas de la manière.
2. Une dépendance de **tâche** : l’ordonnanceur attend que l’initiateur saisisse la plage de dates en suivant une procédure précise (il en crée une aussi vers les participants, pour le format de leurs disponibilités).
3. **Non** : c’est l’initiateur, pas l’ordonnanceur, qui a un enjeu à la présence des participants ; la dépendance reste de l’initiateur vers le participant important.
4. Opportunité : l’initiateur n’a plus à atteindre ce but lui-même. Vulnérabilité : il dépend désormais de la réussite de l’ordonnanceur.
solution.en:
1. A **goal** dependency (MeetingBeScheduled): the initiator delegates scheduling and does not care how it is done.
2. A **task** dependency: the scheduler expects the initiator to enter the date range following a specific procedure (it also creates one towards participants, for the format of their availability).
3. **No**: the initiator, not the scheduler, has a stake in the participants’ attendance; the dependency remains from the initiator to the important participant.
4. Opportunity: the initiator no longer has to achieve this goal itself. Vulnerability: it now depends on the scheduler’s success.

src.quote: The meeting initiator delegates much of the work of meeting scheduling to the meeting scheduler
The scheduler expects the meeting initiator to enter the date range by following a specific procedure
to enter availability information in a particular format. This is modelled as a task dependency on participants
It is the meeting initiator (not the meeting scheduler) who has a stake in having participants attend the meeting
represents an opportunity for the meeting initiator not to have to achieve this goal himself
the meeting initiator would become vulnerable to the failure of the meeting scheduler in achieving this goal

title.fr: Vrai ou faux, format des annales : i*
title.en: True or false, exam format: i*

statement.fr:
« Répondez par VRAI ou FAUX, justifiez si (et seulement si) vous répondez FAUX. » (la question 1 est celle de l’annale 2013 ; les suivantes sont dans son format)
1. (2013 Q3) Les « soft goals » du formalisme i* sont des buts qui ne peuvent jamais être satisfaits puisqu’on n’a pas de critère mesurable.
2. Dans i*, une dépendance de tâche laisse le dependee libre de choisir la manière de faire.
3. Le modèle SD de i* cache le contenu intentionnel de chaque acteur.
4. Dans un modèle SR, une décomposition de tâche donne une alternative parmi d’autres pour atteindre un but.
statement.en:
“Answer TRUE or FALSE, justify if (and only if) you answer FALSE.” (question 1 is from the 2013 exam; the others follow its format)
1. (2013 Q3) Soft goals in the i* framework are goals that can never be satisfied since there is no measurable criterion.
2. In i*, a task dependency leaves the dependee free to choose how to do it.
3. The i* SD model hides the intentional content of each actor.
4. In an SR model, a task decomposition gives one alternative among others to achieve a goal.

hints.fr: Pour chaque énoncé : quelle notion, et quel mot (jamais, libre, cache, alternative) décide ?
hints.en: For each statement: which notion, and which word (never, free, hides, alternative) decides?

solution.fr:
Corrigé **proposé**.
1. **FAUX** : un soft goal n’a pas de critère tranché, mais il est satisfait de façon suffisante (*satisficing*, solutions « good enough ») ; « jamais » est faux.
2. **FAUX** : en dépendance de tâche, la manière est imposée (suivre une procédure précise) ; c’est la dépendance de but qui laisse le choix.
3. **VRAI** : le SD montre les relations entre acteurs et cache leurs constructions intentionnelles internes ; le SR regarde à l’intérieur.
4. **FAUX** : la décomposition énumère les éléments qui composent une routine ; c’est le lien moyens-fins qui relie une fin à un moyen parmi d’autres.
solution.en:
**Proposed** answers.
1. **FALSE**: a softgoal has no clear-cut criterion, but it is satisficed (“good enough” solutions); “never” is false.
2. **FALSE**: in a task dependency, the way is imposed (following a specific procedure); the goal dependency is the one that leaves the choice.
3. **TRUE**: the SD shows relationships among actors and hides their internal intentional constructs; the SR looks inside.
4. **FALSE**: decomposition lists the elements that make up a routine; the means-ends link relates an end to one means among others.

writing.sentence: A soft goal can never be satisfied, so we must ignore it.

explanation.fr: Un soft goal n’est pas satisfait de façon tranchée, mais il peut être *satisficed* (atteint de façon suffisante).
explanation.en: A soft goal is not satisfied in a clear-cut way, but it can be *satisficed* (achieved to a sufficient level).

prompt.fr: En 2-3 phrases anglaises, explique la différence entre une dépendance de but et une dépendance de tâche dans i*.
prompt.en: In 2-3 English sentences, explain the difference between a goal dependency and a task dependency in i*.

writing.modelAnswer: In a goal dependency, the depender only expects the goal to be achieved: it is up to the dependee how to attain it. In a task dependency, the dependee is expected to follow a specific procedure. For example, the meeting scheduler expects the initiator to enter the date range in a specific way.
